newsitem.title: USA: Unigene in $50 million Warner-Lambert deal.
newsitem.headline: Unigene in $50 million Warner-Lambert deal.

text.p: Unigene Laboratories Inc. said Monday it agreed with the Parke-Davis division of Warner-Lambert Co. to co-develop an oral form of a popular drug for the treatment of osteoporosis.
The drug, calcitonin, is only available in injectable and nasal forms, with annual worldwide sales of more than $700 million.

Unigene, a biotechnology company based in Fairfield, N.J., said it would receive $50 million in up-front and milestone payments from the licensing agreement. Warner-Lambert would buy an undisclosed amount of Unigene stock.
Under the terms of the letter of intent, Warner-Lambert would develop and market the product, while Unigene would provide analytical support and would be the exclusive supplier of the raw material.
The parties said they hope to sign a definitive agreement by mid-July.
Unigene's stock rose 25 cents to $5.25 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
